Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called al-An'am (the Cattle), because it deals in detail with the beasts of cattle (al-an'am) in a manner not found in any other surah. It clarifies the beliefs of the polytheists concerning them, their ignorance in seeking nearness to their idols, and what they forbade for themselves of what Allah had provided for them.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Establishing the Oneness of Divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah) for Allah, glorified and exalted be He, through proving His Lordship (rububiyyah) with convincing rational proofs; declaring Allah, exalted be He above all, free from having a consort or offspring; mentioning the signs of His power and oneness in the creation of the heavens, the earth, humankind and animals; that He alone is the One who does this; and refuting the influence of the alleged partners, be they idols, jinn or others; and refuting the claim of the polytheists that Allah instilled in them the doctrine of association (shirk) with the intention of confounding the Messenger ﷺ.

• Establishing prophethood and messengerhood, speaking of revelation, responding to those who deny it and refuting their doubts, explaining the wisdom behind sending the messengers, admonishing those who turn away from the verses of the Qur'an and those who deny the religion, and warning them that what befell the generations before them may befall them, explaining the way of Allah with those who denied the messengers, and His seizing them suddenly while they were heedless, and threatening them with what they will encounter at death, resurrection and the Day of Judgment.

• Affirming the doctrine of resurrection and recompense, diversifying the means of proving it, explaining its wisdom, depicting the situations of the polytheists and their state on the Day of Judgment, rebuking them for their denial of resurrection, and threatening them with punishment.

• Consoling the Prophet ﷺ regarding what he encounters from his people, strengthening him, and comforting him by citing the example of Ibrahim with his father and his people, and that this is the condition of the prophets and messengers before him.

• Discussion of a number of the customs and conditions of the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah), their disputes, and arguing against their foolishness regarding what they forbade for themselves of what Allah had provided, and refuting their claims concerning permitting and forbidding.

• Explaining some legal rulings, such as giving charity from crops and fruits, mentioning the foods that Allah forbade, forbidding killing, and commanding fulfilment of measure and weight.

• Affirming the great Ten Commandments, which combine matters of belief, manners, morals and transactions, that guarantee happiness and stability for the individual and the community; thus they laid a strong foundation for raising the Muslim upon sound belief and noble character, and established the basis for a cohesive Muslim society in which the individual is secure in his blood, his honour and his property.

• Showing Allah's great favour upon the Ummah by sending down the Qur'an as guidance for them, just as He sent down the Book to Musa, and by making them the seal of the righteous nations, and highlighting the virtue of the Qur'an and Islam, and what Allah bestows upon its people of multiplied good deeds.

[The Tafsir]

Praise of Allah through His attributes, all of which are attributes of perfection, and through His outward and inward blessings, religious and worldly, who originated the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and created the darknesses and the light, and that is by the alternation of night and day. In this is an indication of the greatness of Allah, the Exalted, and His sole right to be worshipped, so it is not permissible for anyone to associate others with Him. And despite this clarity, the disbelievers ascribe equals to Allah and associate others with Him.

He is the One who created your father Adam from clay, and then you descended from him. Then He decreed the term of your stay in this worldly life, and He decreed another appointed term, known only to Him, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is the Day of Resurrection. Then, after all this, you still doubt God's power to resurrect after death.

God Almighty is the One truly worthy of worship in the heavens and on the earth. Among the proofs of His divinity is that He knows all that you conceal, O people, and all that you reveal, and He knows all your deeds, whether good or bad. For this reason, He, exalted is He, alone is the God who deserves to be worshipped.

These disbelievers who associate others with Allah, the Exalted, have been given clear proofs and manifest signs of the Oneness of Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and of the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) in his prophethood and in what he brought. Yet as soon as they came, they turned away from accepting them and did not believe in them.

They denied the truth that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought to them and mocked those who called to it, out of ignorance of God and deception by His giving them respite. So they will soon see that what they mocked was indeed the truth and the reality, and God will make clear to the deniers their lie and fabrication, and He will recompense them for it.

Do these people who deny Allah's oneness and that He alone deserves to be worshipped, and who reject His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), not know what befell the nations that denied before them, of destruction and annihilation? We had given them power in the earth in ways We have not given you, O disbelievers, and We bestowed upon them abundant rain and rivers flowing beneath their dwellings, as a means of gradual leading on and respite. Yet they disbelieved in the blessings of Allah and denied the messengers, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We brought into being after them other nations who succeeded them in cultivating the earth?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 7:

And if We had sent down to you, O Messenger, a Book from the heavens on paper, and these polytheists had touched it with their hands, they would have said: "What you have brought, O Messenger, is nothing but clear, evident magic."

The polytheists said: "Why has God not sent down an angel to Muhammad (ﷺ) from the heavens, to confirm him in what he has brought of prophethood?" Had We sent down an angel from the heavens in response to their demand, the matter would have been decided by their destruction, and then they would not be given respite for repentance; for it had already preceded in the knowledge of God that they would not believe.

If We had made the messenger sent to them an angel, since they were not satisfied with Muhammad (ﷺ), We would have made that angel in the form of a human, so that they could hear from him and speak with him; for they would not be able to see the angel in his angelic form. And had the angel come to them in the form of a man, the matter would have been confused for them, just as the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) was confused for them.

When the demand for the angel to be sent down was made in mockery of Muhammad (ﷺ), God Most High showed him that mocking the messengers, peace be upon them, is not a new matter. Rather, it had already occurred from earlier disbelievers toward their prophets, and so the punishment they used to mock and deny would encompass them.

Say, [O Messenger]: "Travel through the earth and then observe how Allah brought about the end of those who denied [the truth]: destruction and disgrace. So beware of the same fate as theirs, and fear that there may befall you the same thing that befell them."

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?" Say: "To Allah. He has prescribed for Himself mercy, as you acknowledge and know. So worship Him alone." He has prescribed for Himself mercy, so He does not hasten to punish His servants. He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, for reckoning and recompense. Those who associated others with Allah have destroyed themselves; they do not affirm the Oneness of Allah, do not believe in His promise and threat, and do not acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

To Allah belongs the dominion of everything in the heavens and the earth, whether at rest or in motion, hidden or manifest. All of them are His servants and creatures, under His dominion, control, and management. He is the All-Hearing of His servants' words and the All-Knowing of their inner thoughts and their deeds.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists who associate others with Allah, the Exalted: "Shall I take as a protector and helper other than Allah, while He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is the One who provides for His creation, while none provides for Him?" Say, [O Messenger]: "Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first of this nation to submit and yield to Him in worship, and I have been forbidden to be among those who associate with Him anything else."

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists who associate others with Allah: "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, by opposing His command and associating others with Him in worship, that a great punishment will befall me on the Day of Resurrection."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 16:

Whoever Allah averts from that severe punishment, He has shown him mercy. And that averting is the clear triumph of being saved from the great punishment.

If Allah afflicts you, O human, with something that harms you, such as poverty or sickness, then there is none who can remove it except Him. And if He touches you with good, such as wealth or health, then there is none who can repel His bounty or prevent His decree. He, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who has power over all things.

Allah, glorified is He, is the Victorious, the Irresistible above His servants. Necks submit to Him, and tyrants are humbled before Him. He is the All-Wise, who places things in their proper places in accordance with His wisdom, the All-Aware, nothing of whose knowledge is hidden. Whoever is characterized by these attributes must not be associated with in worship. This verse affirms Allah's highness above all His creation, an absolute highness befitting His majesty, glorified is He.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: What thing is greatest in testimony to establish the truth of what I have told you, that I am the Messenger of God? Say: "God is a witness between me and you," meaning: He knows what I have brought you and what you are saying to me. "This Qur'an was revealed to me so that I may warn you by it of His punishment, lest it descend upon you, and warn whoever it reaches of the nations." You indeed testify that there are other deities along with God that you associate with Him. Say to them, [O Messenger]: "I do not bear witness to what you have affirmed; rather, God is one God with no partner, and I am free of every partner you worship alongside Him."

Those whom We gave the Torah and the Gospel recognize Muhammad (ﷺ) through his attributes written in their scriptures, just as they recognize their own sons. Just as their sons are not confused in their eyes with others, so too Muhammad (ﷺ) is not confused with anyone else, because of the precision of his description in their books. But they followed their own desires, so they lost themselves when they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in what he brought.

No one is more unjust than the one who fabricates lies against Allah, the Exalted, claiming that He has partners in worship, or alleging that He has a son or a consort, or denies His proofs and evidences with which He supported His messengers, peace be upon them. Indeed, the wrongdoers who invent lies against Allah will not succeed, nor will they attain their aims, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

This is the commentary on Surah al-An'am (6), verse 22, as given in al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the "Simplified Tafsir" produced by King Fahd Complex):

"Let these polytheists who denied the signs of Allah beware of the Day when We will gather them, and then We will say to them: Where are your deities that you used to claim were partners with Allah, that they would intercede for you?"

Then their answer, when they were tested and questioned about their partners, will be nothing but disowning them, and they will swear by Allah, their Lord, that they had not been polytheists who associated anything with Allah.

Reflect, O Messenger, on how these polytheists lied against themselves, when in the Hereafter they will have disowned their polytheism? And what they used to imagine of the intercession of their deities has gone astray and vanished from them.

Among these polytheists there are those who listen to you recite the Qur'an, O Messenger, yet it does not reach their hearts. Because they follow their desires, We have placed coverings over their hearts so that they do not comprehend the Qur'an, and We have placed heaviness and deafness in their ears, so they hear nothing and understand nothing. And if they see the many signs that point to the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ), they do not believe in them. Until, when they come to you, O Messenger, after witnessing the signs that testify to your truthfulness, they dispute with you. Those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah say: "This is nothing but the tales of the ancients, which they have transmitted, having no reality."

These disbelievers forbid people from following Muhammad (ﷺ) and from listening to him, and they keep themselves far away from him. They destroy no one but themselves by turning others away from the way of Allah, and they do not perceive that they are working toward their own destruction.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 27:

If you could see, O Messenger, these polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, you would see a dreadful sight. That will be when they are held back over the Fire and see for themselves the chains and shackles in it, and they will witness with their own eyes those great and terrifying matters. At that point they will say: "Would that we could be returned to the life of this world, so that we might affirm the signs of God and act upon them, and be among the believers."

It is not so; rather, there becomes manifest to them on the Day of Resurrection what they used to know within themselves of the truth of what the messengers brought in this world, even though they used to show their followers the opposite. Had they been returned to the world and granted respite, they would have returned to their obstinate disbelief and denial. Indeed, they are liars in their saying: "If we were returned to the world, we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."
These polytheists, who deny the resurrection, said: "There is only this worldly life that we are in, and we will not be resurrected after we die."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 30:

If only you could see, O Messenger, those who denied the Resurrection when they are held before Allah, the Exalted, for His judgment concerning them on the Day of Resurrection, you would see a most dreadful state. Allah, Mighty and Exalted, will say: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾, that is: Is this Resurrection, which you used to deny in the world, not true? They will say: ﴿Yes, by our Lord, it is true.﴾ Allah, the Exalted, will say: ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾, that is: the punishment that you used to deny in the world, because of your rejection of Allah, the Exalted, and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 31:

The disbelievers who denied resurrection after death have indeed lost, until, when the Resurrection comes and they are confronted with the evil of their final abode, they will call out against themselves in regret over what they squandered during their life in this world, while they carry their sins upon their backs. How evil are the heavy, wretched burdens that they bear!

In most of its conditions, the life of this world is nothing but delusion and falsehood. Righteous deeds for the Hereafter are better for those who fear God, who guard against His punishment by obeying Him and avoiding His disobedience. Will you not then use your reason, O polytheists who are deceived by the adornment of worldly life, so that you put forward what endures ahead of what perishes?

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 33:

We know well that the denial of your people grieves you outwardly. So be patient and at peace, for they do not deny you in the depths of their hearts; rather, they believe in your truthfulness. But out of their wrongdoing and hostility, they reject the clear proofs of your truthfulness, and so they deny you regarding what you have brought.

The Noble Qur'an: Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 34:

Indeed, disbelievers denied messengers before you, whom Allah had sent to their nations, and they were harmed for His sake. They endured patiently for that and persevered in their call and their struggle until the help of Allah came to them. There is none who can alter the words of Allah, and they are what He sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) concerning His promise to him of victory over those who opposed him. Indeed, there has come to you, O Messenger, news of those who were before you among the messengers, and of the victory of Allah that was realized for them, and of the punishment of Allah and His wrath that befell their deniers. So in those messengers who preceded you there is for you an example and a model. In this there is consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ).

If it weighs heavily on you, O Messenger, that these polytheists turn away and refuse to answer your call, then if you are able to dig a tunnel into the earth, or a ladder by which you can ascend into the sky, and bring them a sign and proof for the truth of what you say other than what We have brought them, then do so. Had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon the guidance you are upon and granted them success in faith, but He did not will that, for a wisdom known to Him, glorified is He. So do not be, O Messenger, among those who are ignorant, whose grief has grown intense, and who have been so distressed that it has led them to excessive anguish.

Only those who listen (with acceptance) will respond to you, O Messenger, to what you have called them to of guidance. As for the disbelievers, they are counted among the dead, because true life is only attained through Islam. And the dead, God will bring them out of their graves alive, then they will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection, so that they may be paid in full their reckoning and their recompense.

The Idolaters said, out of obstinacy and arrogance: "Why has God not sent down a sign of the kind that breaks natural custom, one that shows the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ)?" Say to them, O Messenger: God is able to send down a sign upon them, but most of them do not know that the sending down of signs happens only in accordance with His wisdom, exalted is He.

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 38:**

There is no creature that crawls on the earth, or bird that flies in the sky on its wings, except that they are communities like you, alike in their creation. We have not neglected anything in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), but We have recorded it. Then they will all be gathered to their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, and God will call each one to account for what it did.

Those who denied the proofs of Allah, the Exalted, are deaf: they do not hear what would benefit them. They are mute: they do not speak the truth. They are bewildered in darknesses, and they did not choose the path of uprightness. Whomever Allah wills to lead astray, He leads astray, and whomever He wills to guide, He places upon a straight path.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Tell me: if the punishment of Allah comes upon you in this world, or the Hour comes upon you in which you will be resurrected, will you call upon other than Allah there to remove the affliction that has befallen you, if you are truthful in your claim that the deities you worship besides Allah can benefit or harm?"

Rather, there you call upon your Lord, the One who created you and none other, and you seek His aid, and He relieves you of the great affliction that has befallen you, if He wills; for He is capable of everything. And at that time you abandon your idols, your false gods, and those you took as protectors.

And We had certainly sent messengers, O Messenger, to communities of people before you, calling them to Allah, the Exalted, but they denied them. So We afflicted them with adversity in their wealth, through severe poverty and straitened livelihood, and We afflicted them in their bodies with sicknesses and pains, in the hope that they would humble themselves before their Lord and submit to Him alone in worship.

Why did they not, when Our punishment came upon them, humble themselves to Us? But their hearts were hardened, and Satan made their deeds seem fair to them, the sins they were committing and the idolatry they were practising.

So when they abandoned acting on God's commands, turning away from them, We opened up for them the gates of every kind of provision, and replaced their hardship with ease of living and their harm with bodily health, as a gradual leading-on (istidraj) from Us. Then, when they became insolent and took pride in the good things and blessings We had given them, We seized them with punishment suddenly, and then they were in despair, cut off from every good.

Then these people were completely uprooted and destroyed, because they disbelieved in Allah and denied His messengers, so not one of them was left. And praise and thanks are due to Allah, the Exalted—the Creator and Owner of everything—for granting victory to His friends and the destruction of His enemies.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: Tell me, if Allah were to take away your hearing and make you deaf, and take away your sight and make you blind, and seal your hearts so that you no longer understand any speech, what god other than Allah, exalted is He and high, could restore that to you?! Look, [O Messenger], at how We vary the proofs for them, and yet they still turn away from remembrance and reflection.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: Tell me, if the punishment of God were to come upon you suddenly while you are unaware of it, or openly and visibly while you are looking at it, would anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people, who have transgressed the limit by directing worship to other than God Exalted and by denying His messengers?

We send not Our messengers except as bearers of good news to those who obey Us, with lasting bliss, and as warners to those who disobey, with painful punishment. So whoever believes, affirms the messengers, and does righteous deeds, they will have no fear when they meet their Lord, and they will not grieve over anything of the worldly portions that has eluded them.

Those who denied Our signs, from the Qur'an and the miracles, will be struck by punishment on the Day of Resurrection, because of their disbelief and their departure from obedience to God, exalted is He.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "I do not claim that I possess the treasuries of the heavens and the earth, so that I could dispose of them, nor do I claim to know the unseen, nor do I claim to be an angel. I am only a messenger from Allah, following what is revealed to me and conveying its revelation to the people." Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Is the disbeliever, who is blind to the signs of Allah, the Exalted, and therefore does not believe in them, equal to the believer, who has seen the signs of Allah and believed in them? Will you not then reflect upon the signs of Allah, so that you may see the truth and believe in it?"

And warn, O Messenger, with the Qur'an those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord, for they believe in God's promise and His threat. They have no protector other than God to help them, nor any intercessor to intercede for them with Him, the Exalted, so as to deliver them from His punishment, so that perhaps they will become mindful of God (yattaqun Allah) by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

Do not drive away, O Prophet, from your gatherings the weak among the Muslims who worship their Lord at the beginning and end of the day, seeking by their righteous deeds the face of Allah. You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way, and they are not accountable for yours. Their reckoning rests only with Allah. If you were to drive them away, you would be among those who transgress the limits of Allah, those who place a thing in other than its proper place.

And thus Allah, exalted is He, tests some of His servants with others, through the differing shares they receive of provision and of character: He makes some of them rich and some of them poor, some strong and some weak. He makes some of them in need of others as a trial from Him for them. So that the disbelieving rich will say: "Has Allah favoured these weak ones with guidance to Islam from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are thankful for His blessing, so that He guides them to His religion?

When those who believe in Our signs come to you, [O Prophet], say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has decreed mercy upon Himself: whoever among you does evil in ignorance and then repents after that and makes amends, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful." (Qur'an 6:54)

Note: the translation of the verse above is a rendering of its meaning; the commentary below is translated as it stands.

And when those who believed in the signs of Allah, which bear witness to your truthfulness from the Qur'an and other than it, come to you [O Prophet] seeking a ruling about repentance from their previous sins, then honour them by returning their greeting of peace, and give them good news of the vast mercy of Allah. For He, exalted is He, has prescribed for Himself mercy toward His servants out of bounty, that whoever commits a sin out of ignorance on his part, [ignorance] of its consequence and of its necessitating the wrath of Allah, then, every disobedient person towards Allah, whether he errs or does it deliberately, is ignorant in this regard, even if he knows it is forbidden, and then repents after it and persists in doing righteous deeds, then indeed He, may He be exalted, will forgive his sin, for He is Forgiving toward His repentant servants, and Merciful toward them.

And thus do We make the signs clear, just as We have made clear to you, O Messenger, [this guidance]; We set out the clear proofs for every truth that the people of falsehood deny, so that the truth may become evident and the path of the people of falsehood, who oppose the messengers, may be made manifest.

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden me to worship the idols that you worship besides Him. And say to them: I will not follow your desires; I would have strayed from the straight path if I followed your desires, and I am not among those who are guided.

Say, [O Messenger, to these polytheists]: "I am upon clear insight from my Lord's law, which He has revealed to me, namely, the worship of Him alone. But you have denied this. It is not within my power to bring down the punishment you are hastening upon yourselves. The decision regarding its delay rests with none but Allah, the Exalted. He explains the truth with clear explanation, and He is the best of those who decide between truth and falsehood by His judgment and ruling."

Say, O Messenger: If I had the power to send down the punishment you are hastening, I would have sent it upon you, and the matter would have been settled between me and you. But that rests with Allah, the Exalted, and He knows best the wrongdoers who have overstepped their bounds by associating others with Him.

With Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, are the keys of the unseen (mafatih al-ghayb), meaning the treasuries of the unseen, which none knows except Him. Among them are the knowledge of the Hour, the sending down of rain, what is in the wombs, what one will earn in the future, and the place where a person will die. He knows whatever is on land and in the sea, and not a leaf falls from a plant but He knows it. Every grain in the hidden depths of the earth, and every moist and dry thing, is recorded in a clear Book that admits no confusion, namely the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

He it is who takes your souls at night in a manner resembling their taking at death, and He knows what you have earned by your deeds during the day. Then He restores your spirits to your bodies by waking you from sleep during the day, in a manner resembling being brought back to life after death, so that your appointed terms in this world may be fulfilled. Then your return is to Allah, the Exalted, after you are raised from your graves alive. Then He will inform you of what you used to do in your life in this world, and then He will recompense you for it.

Allah, exalted is He, is the Subjugator (al-Qahir) above His servants, with an absolute height above them in every respect, befitting His majesty, glory be to Him. Everything is subdued before His majesty and greatness. He sends upon His servants angels who guard their deeds and record them, until, when death comes to one of them, the Angel of Death (Malak al-Mawt) and his assistants take his soul, and they do not neglect what they have been commanded.

Then these who were taken in death are returned to Allah, their true Master. Verily, to Him belongs the judgment and the decision on the Day of Resurrection among His servants, and He is the swiftest of those who reckon.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Who rescues you from the terrors of the darknesses of land and sea? Is it not Allah, the Exalted, whom you call upon in calamities, humbling yourselves openly and secretly, saying: 'If He rescues us from these terrors, we will surely be among the thankful,' by worshipping Him, the Mighty and Majestic, alone, with no partner."
Say to them, O Messenger: It is Allah alone who rescues you from these fears and from every hardship, yet after that you still associate others with Him in worship.

Say, O Messenger: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone is able to send upon you a punishment from above you, such as stoning or the flood and the like, or from beneath your feet, such as earthquakes and landslides, or to confound your affairs for you, so that you become factions at odds with one another, with some of you killing others. Look, O Messenger, at how We vary Our clear proofs for these polytheists, so that perhaps they will understand and take heed.

The disbelievers among your people, O Messenger, have denied this Qur'an, which is the true Book in everything it brings. Say to them: "I am not a guardian over you, nor one who watches over you; I am only the Messenger of Allah, conveying to you what I have been sent with."

For every news there is a time when it will be settled and reached its end, so the truth will become clear from falsehood. And you will come to know, O disbelievers, the outcome of your affair when God's punishment descends upon you.

And when you see, O Messenger, those polytheists who discuss the verses of the Qur'an with falsehood and mockery, then turn away from them until they move on to some other topic. And if Satan causes you to forget this, then do not sit with that transgressing people after you remember, the people who discussed the verses of God with falsehood.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 69:

And the believers who fear Allah, the Exalted, and so obey His commands and avoid His prohibitions, bear no responsibility whatsoever for the reckoning of Allah concerning those who engage in vain talk and mock the signs of Allah. Rather, it is incumbent upon them to admonish those people, so that they may cease from that false speech, perhaps they will fear Allah, the Exalted.

Leave, O Messenger, those polytheists who took the religion of Islam as play and amusement, mocking the signs of Allah, and whom the life of this world has deceived with its adornments. And remind with the Qur'an these polytheists and others, lest a soul be held in pledge for its sins and its disbelief in its Lord, having no one besides Allah as a helper to aid it, to rescue it from His punishment, nor any intercessor to intercede for it with Him. And if it offers any ransom, no ransom will be accepted from it. Those are the ones who were held in pledge for their sins; for them in the Fire is a drink of extreme heat and a painful punishment, because of their disbelief in Allah, and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and in the religion of Islam.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Shall we invoke, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us, and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us to Islam? Then we would be like one whom the devils have enticed and bewildered on the earth, while he has companions who are rational believers calling him to the right path they follow, yet he refuses." Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Indeed, the guidance of Allah with which He has sent me is the true guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds, by worshipping Him alone without partner, for He is the Lord and Owner of everything."

And thus we are commanded to establish the prayer completely, and to fear Him by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. And He, exalted is He, is the One to whom all creatures will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection.

Allah, glorified is He, is the One who created the heavens and the earth with truth. And mention, O Messenger, the Day of Resurrection, when Allah will say: "Be," and it will be, by His command, in the blink of an eye or even nearer. His word is the complete truth, and sovereignty belongs to Him alone, glorified is He, on the Day when the Angel blows into the "Trumpet" (al-Qarn), the second blast, by which the souls will return to the bodies. He is the One who knows what is hidden from your senses, O people, and what you witness. He is the Wise who places matters in their proper places, the All-Aware of the affairs of His creation. Allah, exalted is He, is the One who is singled out for these matters and others, in beginning and end, in origination and final return. He alone is the One whom the servants must obey in His law, submit to His judgment, and aspire to His good pleasure and forgiveness.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 74:

Recall, O Messenger, the argument of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) with his father Azar, when he said to him: "Do you take idols as gods? I see you and your people in clear error, far from the path of truth."

And thus did We show Abraham (peace be upon him) the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, guiding him to the truth concerning worship: We let him see the great dominion and the dazzling power contained in the heavens and the earth, so that he would be among those firmly established in faith.

When the night grew dark over Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and covered him, he debated with his people, in order to establish for them that their religion was false, for they used to worship the stars. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw a star, and said, drawing his people on in order to bind them to monotheism: "This is my lord." But when the star set, he said: "I do not love those that set."

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 6, verse 77:

When Abraham saw the moon rising, he said to his people, by way of *istidraj al-khasm* (leading the opponent on step by step): "This is my lord." Then, when it set, he said, while in need of the guidance of his Lord: "If my Lord does not guide me to what is right in His Oneness, I will surely be among the people who have gone astray from the right path by worshipping other than God."

When he saw the sun rising, bright, he said to his people: "This is my lord! This is greater than the star and the moon." But when it set, he said to his people: "I am free of what you associate with God, of worshipping idols, stars and images that you worship besides God, exalted is He."

This is a commentary passage from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex). Here is the translation of the text:

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 79:

I have turned my face in worship solely to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining away from polytheism toward monotheism, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.

His people argued with him concerning the Oneness of God, the Exalted. He said: "Do you argue with me about my devotion to God alone in worship, when He has granted me success in knowing His Oneness? If you threaten me with your deities, that they may inflict some harm upon me, then I do not fear them, for they cannot harm me, except if my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then take heed, so that you may know that He alone is the One deserving of worship?"

How could I fear your idols, when you do not fear God, who created you and created the idols you have associated with Him in worship, without any proof from Him for that? Which of the two groups, the group of polytheists or the group of monotheists, has more right to security and safety from the punishment of God? If you know the truth of what I say, then inform me.

Those who affirmed (ṣaddaqū) God and His Messenger, acted according to His law, and did not mix their faith with shirk, for them is security and safety, and they are the ones guided to the path of truth.

That is the argument with which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) confronted his people; it is Our argument, which We guided him to, until their argument was cut off. We raise in rank whomever We will of Our servants, in this world and in the Hereafter. Indeed your Lord is All-Wise in the management of His creation, All-Knowing of them.

We bestowed Our favour upon Ibrahim (peace be upon him) by granting him Ishaq as a son and Ya'qub as a grandson, and We guided each of them to the path of righteousness. Likewise, We guided Nuh, before Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub, to the truth. Likewise, We guided to the truth from among the descendants of Nuh: Dawud, Sulayman, Ayyub, Yusuf, Musa and Harun (peace be upon them all). And just as We rewarded these prophets for their good deeds, We reward every doer of good.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 6, verse 85:

And likewise We guided Zakariyya, Yahya, Isa, and Ilyas. All of these were prophets, peace be upon them, and all were among the righteous.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 86:

And We guided Isma'il, al-Yasa' (Elisha), Yunus (Jonah), and Lut (Lot). We preferred all of these messengers over the people of their times.

And thus did We guide to the truth whomever We willed of the fathers of these people, their offspring, and their brothers. We chose them for Our religion and for conveying Our message to those to whom We sent them, and We guided them to a correct path, without crookedness in it, which is the Oneness of Allah, the Exalted, and His being declared free of association with partners in worship (shirk).

That guidance is the success granted by Allah, who grants it to whom He wills of His servants. Had these prophets associated partners with Allah—supposing it hypothetically—their deeds would have been nullified, because Allah does not accept any deed alongside shirk.

Those are the prophets whom We favored with guidance and prophethood. They are the ones to whom We gave the Book, such as the scrolls of Ibrahim, the Torah of Musa, the Psalms of Dawud, and the Injil of Isa, and We gave them understanding of these books and chose them to convey Our revelation. So if the disbelievers of your people, O Messenger, deny the verses of this Qur'an, then We have guided to believe in them and to fulfill their rights a people other than them, namely the Muhajirun and the Ansar and those who follow them until the Day of Resurrection, who are not disbelievers in them, but rather believers in them, acting upon what they indicate.

Those prophets mentioned are the ones whom God Almighty guided to His true religion. So follow their guidance, O Messenger, and tread their path. Say to the polytheists: "I do not ask you for any worldly reward in return for conveying Islam. My reward is only from God." And Islam is nothing but a call to all people to the straight path, and a reminder to you and to everyone like you who remains upon falsehood, so that you may take heed of what benefits you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 91:

The polytheists did not venerate Allah with the veneration due to Him, when they denied that Allah, exalted is He, had sent down to any human being anything of His revelation. Say to them, O Messenger: If the matter is as you claim, then who sent down the Book that Moses brought to his people as a light and guidance for mankind? Then the address turned to the Jews, rebuking them, with His saying: ﴿You make it into scattered pages, showing some of them and concealing much of them﴾. Among what they concealed was the information about the description and prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). And Allah taught you, O assembly of Arabs, through the Qur'an—which He sent down to you, containing the report of those before you and those after you, and what will happen after your death—what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers. Say: Allah is the One who sent it down. Then leave these people in their false talk, plunging and playing.

This Qur'an is a Book We have sent down to you, O Messenger, abundantly beneficial, confirming the truth of the scriptures revealed before it and that they are from Allah. We sent it down so that you may warn with it of the punishment of Allah and His might, the people of Makkah and those around it from the peoples of all the regions of the earth. As for those who believe in the Hereafter, they believe that the Qur'an is the speech of Allah, and they guard the establishment of the prayer at its appointed times.

Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah, or claims, "Allah has not sent down any revelation," or who falsely claims that Allah has revealed to him when He has revealed nothing to him, or who claims, "I can send down the like of what Allah has sent down"? If you could only see, O Messenger, these transgressors in the agonies of death, when the angels are stretching out their hands [saying], "Release your souls! Today you will be recompensed with the humiliating punishment, because you used to speak falsely about Allah and were arrogant toward His signs and toward submitting to His messengers."

And indeed you have come to Us alone, for reckoning and recompense, just as We created you the first time, barefoot and naked, and you have left behind you what We had bestowed upon you in the world, of wealth you were proud of. And We do not see with you in the Hereafter your idols which you used to believe would intercede for you, and which you claimed were partners with Allah in worship. Your bonds with one another that existed in the world have been severed, and what you used to claim has vanished from you, that your gods were partners with Allah in worship. And it has become clear that you are the losers, losing your own selves, your families, and your wealth.

Indeed, Allah splits the grain and the date-stone: from the grain He brings forth the crop, and from the date-stone He brings forth the tree. He brings the living out of the dead, such as a human or an animal out of a sperm-drop, and brings the dead out of the living, such as a sperm-drop out of a human or an animal. ﴿That is Allah﴾, i.e., the One who does this is Allah alone, who has no partner, the One deserving of worship. ﴿So how are you turned away from the truth toward falsehood, so that you worship other than Him?﴾

And God, glorified and exalted is He, is the One who splits the brightness of dawn from the darkness of night, and made the night a place of rest, in which whoever is worn out by the day may dwell and take his share of repose. He made the sun and the moon run in their orbits by a precise, measured reckoning that never changes and never falters. That is the decree of the Almighty (al-'Aziz), whose authority is mighty, the All-Knowing (al-'Alim), who knows the interests of His creation and manages their affairs. Al-'Aziz and al-'Alim are among God's Most Beautiful Names (al-asma' al-husna), and they point to the perfection of might and knowledge.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 6:97 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar.

God, glory be to Him, is the One who made the stars for you, O people, as signs by which you find your way through the paths at night when you go astray, because of the intense darkness on land and sea. We have indeed made the clear proofs explicit, so that those among you who possess knowledge of God and His law may reflect upon them.

Allah, glorified is He, is the One who began your creation, O people, from Adam (peace be upon him). He created him from clay. Then you became offspring and progeny from him. He made for you a settled place in which you settle, which is the wombs of women, and a place of deposit in which you are kept, which is the loins of men. We have made the proofs clear and distinguished the evidences, and We have made them firm, for a people who understand where the proofs lie and where the lessons are found.

Allah, glorified is He, is the One who sent down water from the clouds, and by it brought forth the vegetation of every thing. He brought forth from the vegetation green crops and trees; then He brought forth from the crops grain, layered one upon another, like the ears of wheat, barley and rice (al-Urz). And from the spathe of the date palm (ṭalʿ al-nakhl), which is the sheath in which the first fruit of the date palm develops, He brought forth clusters (ʿudhūq) bearing dates (al-ruṭab), within easy reach. Glorified is He, He also brought forth gardens of grapes, and the olive and pomegranate trees, which resemble one another in their leaves but differ in their fruit in shape, taste and nature. Look, O people, at the fruit of this vegetation when it bears fruit, and at its ripening and its maturity when it reaches maturity. Indeed, in that, O people, are signs of the perfect power of the Creator of these things, and His wisdom and His mercy, for a people who believe in Him, may He be exalted, and act according to His law.

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 100:**

These polytheists made the jinn partners with God, the Exalted, in worship, believing that they benefit or harm. God created them, and created what they worship, from nothing. He alone is independent in creation, so He alone must be independent in worship, with no partner. These polytheists lied against God, the Exalted, when they attributed sons and daughters to Him, out of ignorance of the perfect attributes that are due to Him. He is exalted and high above the lie and fabrication that the polytheists attribute to Him.

Almighty God is He who brought into being the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, without any prior pattern. How could He have a son when He has had no consort? Exalted is God far above what the polytheists say, a great exaltation. He is the One who created every thing from non-existence, and nothing of the affairs of creation is hidden from Him.

That is Allah, your Lord (O polytheists), there is no deity worthy of worship but Him, the Creator of all things. So submit to Him and obey Him in worship. And He is the Guardian over all things, the Trustee who manages the affairs of His creation.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 6:103 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

No vision can encompass Allah, although the believers will see their Lord in the Hereafter without encompassing Him. He, glorified is He, perceives all vision and encompasses it, knows it as it truly is. He is al-Latif (the Subtly Kind) toward His allies, who knows the finest details of things, and al-Khabir (the All-Aware), who knows their inner realities.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "There have certainly come to you clear proofs (baraheen) from your Lord, by which you may see guidance from error, [proofs] contained in the Qur'an and brought by the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. So whoever perceives these proofs and believes in what they indicate, the benefit of that is for himself, and whoever does not see the guidance after the proof has been established against him, it is upon himself that he has inflicted [the harm]. I am not a guardian over you, to count your deeds; I am only a messenger who conveys. And Allah guides whom He wills and leaves astray whom He wills, according to His knowledge and wisdom."

And thus We explain, in this Qur'an, the clear proofs to the polytheists concerning the matter of Tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, and the Resurrection (al-Ma'ad); We explain to them proofs regarding everything they were ignorant of. Then they say, at that point, falsely: "You have learned it from the People of the Book." ﴿And thus We differentiate the verses, so that the truth may be made clear﴾, for a people who know it, so they accept it and follow it, and they are the believers in the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ), and in what was revealed to him.

Follow, O Messenger, what has been revealed to you from your Lord, its commands and prohibitions, the greatest of which is the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, and calling to Him. Do not concern yourself with the obstinacy of the polytheists and their false claims.

If Allah had willed that these polytheists not associate partners with Him, they would not have associated any. But He, exalted is He, knows what will come about of their bad choosing and their following of their deviant desires. And We have not made you, O Messenger, a watcher over them to guard their deeds, nor are you a guardian over them to manage their affairs.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 108:

Do not revile, O Muslims, the idols that the polytheists worship, lest that lead to their reviling Allah out of ignorance and transgression without knowledge, by way of blocking the means (sadd al-dhari'a, blocking the pathways that lead to what is forbidden). Just as We made their evil deeds appealing to these people as a punishment for their bad choice, We have made appealing to every nation its own deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, all of them, and He will inform them of the deeds they used to do in the world, and then He will recompense them for them.

The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 109:

These polytheists swore solemn oaths: "If Muhammad brings us a striking sign, we will surely believe in what he brings." Say, O Messenger: The bringing of extraordinary miracles is only from Allah, the Exalted; He is the One able to bring them whenever He wills. And what will make you aware, O believers, that these miracles, if they come, will not be believed by these polytheists?

We will turn their hearts and their sight away from the truth, so that they cannot benefit from the signs of Allah. Thus they will not believe in them, just as they did not believe in the verses of the Qur'an when they were first revealed. We will leave them wandering bewildered in their rebellion against Allah, unable to find the way to truth and right.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 111:

If We had answered the request of these polytheists, sent down to them the angels from the sky, brought the dead to life for them so that they spoke to them, and gathered for them everything they asked for, witnessing it face to face, they still would not have believed in what you call them to, O Messenger, nor acted upon it, except for those whom Allah wills to guide. But most of these disbelievers are ignorant of the truth that you have brought from Allah, exalted is He.

And just as We have tested you, O Messenger, with enemies among the polytheists, We tested all the prophets (peace be upon them) with enemies from the rebellious leaders of their peoples and enemies from the rebellious jinn, some of whom inspire to others embellished speech, adorned with falsehood, so that its hearer may be deceived by it and go astray from the way of Allah. Had your Lord—exalted is He—willed, He would have prevented them from that enmity, but it is a trial from Allah. So leave them and what they fabricate of lies and falsehood.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 6:113 from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (King Fahd Complex):

"And so that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may earn what they are earning of evil deeds. And in this is a great warning for them."

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: "Shall I seek a judge other than Allah, when He is my Lord and your Lord? It is He who has sent down to you the Qur'an, made clear, containing the decision regarding that about which you dispute concerning me and you?" And the Children of Israel, to whom Allah gave the Torah and the Gospel, know with certain knowledge that this Qur'an has been sent down to you, O Messenger, from your Lord in truth. So do not be among those who doubt in anything of what We have revealed to you.

And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled, [meaning the Qur'an], in truth in its reports and statements, and in justice in its rulings, so none can alter His perfect words. And Allah, exalted is He, is the All-Hearing of what His servants say, the All-Knowing of their inner and outer affairs.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 116:

"And if you were to obey most of those on earth, O Messenger, they would lead you astray from the religion of God. They follow nothing but what they assumed to be true through their blind imitation of their forefathers, and they are nothing but conjecturing and lying."

This is the commentary text of al-Tafsir al-Muyassar on Surah al-An'am (6), verse 117. Translating the passage:

Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of those who stray from the path of right guidance, and He is more knowing than you and them of those who remain upon uprightness and rectitude. Nothing about them is hidden from Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 118:

﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in the clear proofs of Allah.﴾

And what is it that prevents you, O Muslims, from eating of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, when Allah, glorified is He, has already explained to you everything that He has forbidden to you? However, what necessity compels you to, because of famine, from what is forbidden to you, such as carrion, is permitted to you. Indeed, many of the misguided lead others astray from the way of Allah, out of ignorance, by making lawful what is unlawful and making unlawful what is lawful according to their own desires. Indeed, your Lord, O Messenger, is most knowing of those who transgress their limits in this matter, and He is the One who will take their reckoning and recompense them.

Abandon, O people, all acts of disobedience, whether they are committed openly or in secret. Indeed, those who commit acts of disobedience will be punished by their Lord, because of the evil deeds they used to perform.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 121:

Do not eat, O Muslims, of the slaughtered animals over which the name of Allah was not mentioned at the time of slaughter, such as carrion and what is sacrificed to idols and jinn, and other such things. Indeed, eating from those slaughtered animals is a departure from the obedience of Allah, the Exalted. Indeed, the rebellious jinn (marada al-jinn) inspire their allies among the devils of mankind with doubts concerning the prohibition of eating carrion, so they command them to say to the Muslims in their disputes with them: "By your not eating carrion, you do not eat what Allah has killed, while you eat what you slaughter yourselves." And if you obey them, O Muslims, in permitting carrion, then you and they are equal in polytheism.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 122:

Is one who was dead in misguidance, lost and bewildered, then We gave him life through faith, guided him to it, and enabled him to follow Our messengers, so that he now lives in the lights of guidance, like one who is in ignorance, desires and scattered misguidance, unable to find a way out and with no means of deliverance from what he is in? They are not alike. Just as We forsook this disbeliever who argues with you, O believers, and made his evil deeds seem good to him so that he sees them as fine, We have made the evil deeds of the deniers seem good to them, so that they thereby deserve the punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 123:

And like what happened from the leaders of the disbelievers in Makkah in barring (people) from the religion of Allah, We placed in every town criminals whose great ones were their leaders, so that they would scheme in it by barring (people) from the religion of Allah. But they scheme only against themselves, and they do not perceive it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 124:

When a clear proof of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ came to these polytheists of Makkah, some of their leaders said: "We will never believe in his prophethood until Allah gives us prophethood and miracles like those given to His earlier messengers." Allah the Exalted replied to them with His words: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾, meaning: He knows best those who are fit to bear His message and convey it to people. ﴿Humiliation will befall these tyrants﴾, and for them there is a painful punishment in the Fire of Hell, because of their plotting against Islam and its people.

Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his chest to accept the truth, expanding it to Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah) and faith; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his chest extremely constricted, shrinking from accepting guidance, like the state of one who ascends into the upper layers of the atmosphere, so that he is afflicted with severe tightness in breathing. Just as Allah makes the chests of the disbelievers extremely tight and constricted, likewise He sends punishment upon those who do not believe in Him.
This that We have made clear to you, O Messenger, is the path leading to the pleasure of your Lord and His Garden. We have made the proofs clear for those among people of sound minds who take heed.

For those who remember, with their Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, on the Day of Resurrection there is the abode of peace and security from every hardship, which is Paradise. He, glorified is He, is their helper and protector, as a recompense to them for their righteous deeds.

And remember, O Messenger, the Day when Allah will gather together the disbelievers and their allies from among the devils of the jinn. He will say: "O assembly of jinn, you have led astray many of mankind." And their allies from among the disbelieving humans will say: "Our Lord, some of us have benefited from others, and we have reached the term You appointed for us," meaning the end of our worldly life. Allah the Exalted will say to them: "The Fire is your abode," that is, the place where you will remain, "abiding therein forever," except for those whom Allah wills not to abide forever therein, from among the sinful monotheists. Indeed your Lord is All-Wise in His management and His creation, All-Knowing of all the affairs of His servants.

Just as We let the devils among the jinn dominate the disbelieving humans, so that they became their allies, so too do We let the wrongdoers among humankind dominate one another in this world, because of the sins they commit.

O you polytheists, among the jinn and mankind! Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves? —and the apparent wording of the texts indicates that the messengers were from mankind only— who relate to you My clear signs, which contain the commands and prohibitions, and the explanation of good and evil, and who warn you of meeting My punishment on the Day of Resurrection? These polytheists, from mankind and the jinn, will say: "We bear witness against ourselves that Your messengers did convey to us Your signs, and warned us of the meeting of this day of ours," but we denied them. The adornment of the worldly life deceived these polytheists, and they bore witness against themselves that they had been deniers of the oneness of Allah the Exalted and deniers of His messengers, peace be upon them.

We have established the proof against both jinn and humankind by sending the messengers and revealing the scriptures, so that no one would be taken to account for his wrongdoing when no call had reached him. Rather, We have established the proof against the nations, and We never punished anyone except after sending messengers to them.

For every doer, whether in obedience to Allah the Exalted or in disobedience to Him, there are degrees (of reward or punishment) according to his deeds, which Allah will make reach him, and for which He will recompense him. And your Lord, O Messenger, is not unaware of what His servants do.

Your Lord, O Messenger, the One who commanded people to worship Him, is the Self-Sufficient alone, and all of His creation is in need of Him. He, glorified is He, is possessed of vast mercy. Were He to will, He would destroy you, and bring into existence other people after you, to succeed you after your passing away, and who would act in obedience to Him, Exalted is He, just as He brought you into being from the offspring of other peoples who were before you.

Indeed, what your Lord promises you—O polytheists—of punishment for your disbelief will surely befall you, and you will never escape your Lord by fleeing; He is able to bring you back, even if you have become dust and bones.

Say, [O Messenger]: "O my people, act according to your position, and I am acting according to mine. You will soon know, when the punishment befalls you, to whom the good final outcome belongs. Indeed, no one who transgresses his limits and wrongs himself, by associating partners with God, will attain the good pleasure of God and Paradise."

The idolaters assigned to God—exalted is He—a portion of what He created of crops, fruits and livestock, which they would offer to guests and the needy. They also set aside another share of these things for their partners among the idols and altars. Whatever was designated for their partners would reach them alone and would not reach God, while whatever was designated for God, exalted is He, would be passed on to their partners. Evil is the judgment of this people and their division.

And just as Satan made attractive to the polytheists that they should assign to God a share of the crops and livestock, and to their partners a share, the devils have also made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children out of fear of poverty; so that they might bring those fathers to ruin by killing the soul which God has forbidden to kill except by right, and so that they might confuse their religion for them, so that it becomes obscure, and they go astray and perish. Had God willed that they not do that, they would not have done it; but He decreed it, for His knowledge of their evil state and their final outcome. So leave them, O Messenger, to themselves regarding the falsehoods they invent, for God will judge between you and them.

The Polytheists said: "These are livestock and tilled crops that are forbidden; none may eat them except whomever they permit, according to their claim, from among the custodians of the idols and others." And they said: "These are livestock whose backs have been forbidden, so it is not permitted to ride them or to load them under any circumstances." And they said: "These are livestock upon which they do not mention the name of God, Most High, in any of their affairs." They did this as a lie fabricated by them against God. God will repay them for what they used to invent of lies against Him, glory be to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 139:

The polytheists said: "What is in the wombs of the livestock is permitted for our men and forbidden for our women if it is born alive, but they share it if it is born dead." God will punish them, since they legislated for themselves permitting and forbidding that God had not authorized. He, the Exalted, is wise in managing the affairs of His creation, and knowing of them.

Those who killed their children out of foolishness, through weakness of intellect and ignorance, and who forbade what Allah had provided for them, inventing lies against Allah, have certainly lost and perished. They have strayed far from the truth, and they were not among the people of guidance and rectitude. So the lawful is what Allah has made lawful, and the unlawful is what Allah has made unlawful, and no one among His creatures, whether an individual or a group, has the right to legislate for His servants what Allah has not permitted.

Almighty God, He it is Who brought into being for you gardens, some of them trellised and some not trellised but standing upon their stalks, like the palm trees and the crops, with varied flavors; and the olive and the pomegranate, similar in appearance and differing in their fruit and flavor. Eat, O people, of their fruit when it bears fruit, and give its obligatory zakat on the day of its harvesting and reaping, and do not exceed the limits of moderation in spending wealth, eating food, and other things. Indeed, He, the Exalted, does not love those who exceed His limits by spending wealth in other than its proper place.

And He produced from the livestock that which is fit for carrying loads, owing to its size and height, such as camels, and among them that which is fit for other than carrying, owing to its smallness and nearness to the ground, such as cattle and sheep. "Eat of what Allah has permitted you and provided you from these livestock, and do not forbid what Allah has made lawful of them, following the footsteps of Satan, as the polytheists did. Indeed, Satan is an open enemy to you."

These are the livestock animals that Allah gave to His servants: camels, cattle, and sheep and goats, eight kinds in all. Four of them are from sheep and goats: the male and female of the sheep (ḍaʼn), and the male and female of the goat (maʻz). Say, O Messenger, to those polytheists: Has Allah forbidden the two males of the sheep and goats? If they say, "Yes," then they have lied in that, for they do not forbid every male of the sheep and goats. And say to them: Has Allah forbidden the two females of the sheep and goats? If they say, "Yes," then they have also lied, for they do not forbid every female of the young of the sheep and goats. And say to them: Has Allah forbidden what the wombs of the two females of the sheep and goats contain of the unborn young? If they say, "Yes," then they have also lied, for they do not forbid every unborn young of these. Inform me with knowledge that supports the validity of what you have adopted, if you are truthful in what you attribute to your Lord.

The other four kinds: they are two of the camel, male and female, and two of the cattle, male and female. Say, O Messenger, to those polytheists: Has God forbidden the two males or the two females? Or has He forbidden what the wombs of the two females contain, whether male or female? Or were you, O polytheists, present when God enjoined upon you this prohibition concerning the livestock? So who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God, to lead people astray from the path of guidance through his ignorance? Indeed, God does not guide to rectitude those who transgress their limits, who lie against their Lord and lead people astray.

Say, [O Messenger]: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it of what you claim to be forbidden from the cattle, except that it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure, or that which was slaughtered in a way that constitutes disobedience to Allah, the Exalted; such as when the animal slaughtered has had the name of other than Allah invoked over it at the time of slaughter." Whoever is compelled to eat from these forbidden things, by severe hunger, without seeking to eat them for pleasure and without exceeding the limit of necessity, then indeed Allah is Forgiving toward him and Merciful to him. And it was established afterward, by the Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition), the prohibition of every animal with fangs among the predators, every bird with talons, the domestic donkeys, and the dogs.

Recall, O Messenger, to these polytheists what We forbade to the Jews of the cattle and birds: it is every animal that does not have split hooves, such as camels and ostriches, and the fat of cattle and sheep, except what clings to their backs or intestines, or is mixed with the bone of the rump and the flank, and the like. That prohibition upon the Jews was a punishment from Us for them because of their evil deeds, and indeed We are truthful in what We have told you about them.

If they deny you, [O Messenger], then those who oppose you among the polytheists, the Jews, and others, say to them: your Lord, may He be exalted, is possessed of vast mercy, yet His punishment is not averted from the people who committed crimes, who earned sins and perpetrated evil deeds. And in this is a warning to them for their opposition to the Messenger (ﷺ).

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 148:

Those who associated partners with Allah will say: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated partners with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything apart from Him." Such was the case before them, and their denial was similar. Allah responded to them by making clear that this doubt had been raised by the disbelievers before them, who denied the call of their messengers and persisted in that until the punishment of Allah befell them. Say to them, O Messenger: "Do you have any sound knowledge regarding what you have forbidden of the cattle and the crops, and regarding what you claim, that Allah has willed disbelief for you, approved it from you, and loved it for you, so that you may bring it forth to us?" You only follow conjecture in matters of this religion, and you are only lying.
Say, O Messenger, to them: To God, exalted is He, belongs the conclusive proof which cuts off your assumptions. Had He willed, He would have guided you all to the path of uprightness.

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Bring forward your witnesses who will testify that Allah is the One who prohibited what you have prohibited of crops and livestock." If they testify [falsely], then do not affirm them as witnesses, and do not follow those who have made their desires their judge, who denied the signs of Allah in their claim to prohibit what Allah has permitted and to permit what Allah has prohibited. Do not follow those who do not believe in the Hereafter and do not work for it, and those who associate others with their Lord, worshipping alongside Him something other than Him.

Say, [O Messenger], to them: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him in worship, but direct all kinds of worship to Him alone, such as fear, hope, supplication, and other things; that you be good to your parents through righteousness, supplication, and the like of kindness; that you do not kill your children out of fear of poverty that has befallen you, for it is God who provides for you and for them; that you do not approach the indecencies, whether apparent or hidden; and that you do not kill the soul which God has forbidden to be killed, except by right. That is, in the case of retribution against the killer, or adultery after being married, or apostasy from Islam. That is what He has mentioned to you of what He has forbidden you, and what He has enjoined upon you to avoid, and what your Lord has commanded and charged you with, so that you may understand His commands and prohibitions."

Do not approach the property of an orphan, O guardians, except in the way that is best for it and makes it beneficial to him, until he reaches maturity and becomes mature in judgment. When he reaches that stage, hand over his property to him. And give full measure and weight with justice, the justice by which complete fulfilment is achieved. If you have exerted your utmost effort, there is no blame on you for any shortfall that may occur, for Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity. When you speak, then be careful in your speech to uphold justice, without deviating from the truth in a report, a testimony, a judgment or an intercession, even if the one concerned by the statement is a relative of yours. So do not incline with him unjustly. And fulfil the covenant of Allah that He has enjoined upon you, namely adherence to His law. That is what has been recited to you of the rulings, which your Lord has enjoined upon you, in the hope that you will remember the outcome of your affair.

And among what Allah has enjoined upon you is that this Islam is the straight path of Allah, so follow it, and do not follow the paths of misguidance, for they will scatter you and turn you away from the way of Allah, which is straight. That turning toward the straight path is what Allah has enjoined upon you, so that you may guard yourselves against His punishment by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

Then say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, is the One who gave Moses the Torah, as a completion of His favor upon the good-doers among his people, and as a detailed explanation of everything pertaining to their religion, and as guidance and a sign pointing to the straight path, and as mercy for them, in the hope that they would believe in the resurrection after death, the reckoning and the recompense, and act accordingly.

This Qur'an is a Book We have sent down upon our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Its good is abundant, so follow it in what it commands and forbids, and fear Allah, lest you oppose any of its commands, in the hope that you may be shown mercy, be saved from His punishment, and attain His reward.

We revealed this Qur'an, so that you (disbelieving Arabs) would not say: "The Book was only sent down from heaven to the Jews and the Christians, and we were occupied from studying their books, and we have no knowledge or understanding of them."

Lest you say, O polytheists: "Had a Book been sent down to us, as it was sent down to the Jews and the Christians, we would have been more guided upon the path of truth than they." But there has now come to you a Book in your own tongue, clear in Arabic, and that is a manifest proof from your Lord, a guidance to the path of truth, and a mercy to this nation. So none is more unjust and more transgressive than one who denies the proofs of Allah and turns away from them! As for those who turn away, We shall requite them with a severe punishment in the Fire of Hell, because of their turning away from Our signs and their barring others from Our way.

Do the ones who turned away and barred others from the path of God await anything but that the Angel of Death and his helpers come to them to seize their souls, or that your Lord comes—O Messenger—to judge between His servants on the Day of Resurrection, or that some of the portents of the Hour and its signs that indicate its coming appear, namely the rising of the sun from its west? On the day that happens, faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before, nor will good deeds be accepted from a soul that did not do righteous deeds before that. Say to them, O Messenger: "Wait for that to come, so that you may know the one who is right from the one who is false, and the evildoer from the doer of good. We too are waiting."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 159:

Indeed, those who split their religion and became sects, after they had been united in the Tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness) of Allah and in acting upon His law, becoming factions and parties. Verily, you, O Messenger, are free of them. Their affair rests with Allah, the Exalted; then He will inform them of their deeds, rewarding whoever among them repents and does good with His bounty, and punishing the evildoer for his evil.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 6, verse 160:

Whoever comes before his Lord on the Day of Resurrection with a good deed from the righteous deeds, he will have ten good deeds like it. And whoever comes before his Lord with an evil deed, he will not be punished except with its like, and they will not be wronged even an atom's weight.

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to the straight path that leads to His Paradise. It is the religion of Islam, which upholds the affairs of both this world and the Hereafter. It is the religion of monotheism, the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was not one of those who associated anything with Allah besides Him."

Say, [O Messenger], to these polytheists: "Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice (nusuk), that is, my slaughtering for Allah alone, not for idols, nor for the dead, nor for the jinn, nor for anything else that you slaughter for other than Allah and in other than His name, as you do, and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds."

He has no partner in His divinity, nor in His lordship, nor in His names and attributes. With this pure monotheism my Lord, exalted is He, has commanded me, and I am the first of this community to acknowledge and submit to God.

Say, [O Messenger]: Shall I seek a deity other than Allah, when He is the Creator of everything, its Owner, and its Manager? No one commits an evil deed except that its sin falls upon him, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return on the Day of Resurrection, and He will inform you of that about which you used to differ concerning matters of religion.

And Allah, glorified is He, is the One who made you successors (khulafa’, sing. khalifa) to those who came before you on earth, after Allah had destroyed them, and He made you its inheritors, so that you might populate it after them through obedience to your Lord. He raised some of you above others in provision and strength, by degrees, in order to test you regarding what He has given you of His blessings, so that those who are thankful may be distinguished from others among the people. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment for whoever disbelieves in Him and disobeys Him, and indeed He is most forgiving to whoever believes in Him, does righteous deeds, and repents from the grave sins (al-mubiqat), and most merciful to him. Al-Ghafur (the Oft-Forgiving) and al-Rahim (the Most Merciful) are two noble names among the Most Beautiful Names of Allah.
